dropzones.name: Jelgava former dropzone
dropzones.status_evidence: The municipality's own 2023 industrial-park strategy calls the site a 'former airfield', a degraded, overgrown, unbuilt territory not in economic use, and English Wikipedia says the skydiving operation shut down in 2010. Skydive Latvia operates at Limbaži instead. One correction to Codex's evidence: the municipality later terminated the SP Austrumi solar-park contract because construction never began, so the site is disused rather than built over; that does not change the closure.

sources.what: Opened municipal announcement dated 27 January 2023: clearance and redevelopment of the former airfield, including a nearly 112-hectare solar park.
Opened regional heritage page: historical Rīgas Aeroklubs parachuting, runway dismantling preventing aviation, and industrial-park use.

Jelgava municipality, Zemgale industrial park strategy (July 2023): 'bijušā lidlauka teritorija', degraded, overgrown and unbuilt, the only large free municipal industrial territory not yet in economic use.
Municipality terminated the solar-park building-rights contract because no construction had started (late 2023).
Older municipal newspaper article (prices in lats, so before 2014) confirming the site was once an active weekend dropzone.
